headline: China is rapidly expanding the Lop Nur flight test complex in Xinjiang, a highly restricted facility used for testing advanced and experimental military aircraft. Lop Nur has previously been associated with testing China's J-36 and J-XDS sixth generation fighter designs. The latest construction is particularly notable because the new southern hangars are substantially wider than typical tactical-aircraft shelters. The War Zone assesses that the facilities could eventually support larger aircraft, including China's H-20 stealth bomber, which has yet to publicly appear. However, the article emphasizes that there is currently no evidence the H-20 is headed to Lop Nur, making that an assessment rather than a confirmed development. The broader takeaway is that Lop Nur is evolving from a relatively austere test airfield into a major, high capacity test center for China's next generation aerospace programs, with the pace of construction accelerating significantly in 2025–26. Source: https://www.twz.com/news-features/chinas-area-51-is-undergoing-a-massive-expansion

So far, Palisa states, evidence does not suggest that Russian ground forces are massing in Belarus and Western Russia for such an operation, but that Ukraine’s priority is to “prevent the creation of conditions for the Russians to be able to launch any offensive actions at all.” At the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, Russian ground forces attempted an offensive on Kyiv, launched in part from nearby Belarus, but ultimately became bogged down due to strikes on logistics lines before being crushed and repelled by the Armed Forces of Ukraine. Since then, the Russian Army has been significantly weakened while the Ukrainian Army has only grown stronger, even making small gains against Russia in Eastern Ukraine.

headline: The Iran war is creating growing concerns about U.S. munitions inventories and the ability to respond to a major contingency involving China or Russia. According to U.S. officials cited by the Wall Street Journal, PAC-3 Patriot interceptors and ATACMS missiles in Europe have fallen to “beyond critical” levels. Other precision weapons and guided rockets have also been drawn down, while THAAD interceptors and counter-drone systems have been moved from Europe to the Middle East. By mid-July, U.S. forces had reportedly expended approximately 1,700 Patriot interceptors, 200 THAAD interceptors and 150 Navy Standard Missiles during the Iran conflict. Iran has launched more than 1,500 ballistic missiles and 6,000 large drones during the war. The depletion is affecting U.S. planning. European Command has reportedly adjusted operational plans, while officials have previously acknowledged that current inventories could constrain the ability to execute contingency plans for Taiwan. The problem is compounded by production timelines. Replenishing some advanced interceptors and missiles could take years, even as European allies face delays receiving weapons they have already purchased. The White House and Pentagon dispute the characterization of a broader U.S. munitions shortage, saying current inventories remain sufficient to meet America's strategic objectives. NATO likewise says the alliance retains enough air-defense munitions for its defense. Source: https://www.wsj.com/politics/national-security/drain-on-u-s-munitions-from-iran-war-raises-fears-over-ability-to-deter-china-russia-c7d4512d?st=qhre54

headline: President Trump says the U.S. has secured majority control over a joint venture covering more than 65 billion barrels of proven Venezuelan oil reserves, following the administration’s effort to bring American energy companies back into Venezuela. Under the reported arrangement, Venezuela’s interim government granted the venture a 100-year concession to operate the affected oil fields. The U.S. government would control 55% of the venture, through a combination of equity and the ability to acquire oil at cost. The Trump administration says the arrangement could bring nearly $100 billion in private investment, increase U.S. oil supplies and eventually reduce energy prices. The administration also says the deal comes at no cost to U.S. taxpayers. The agreement covers roughly one-fifth of Venezuela’s more than 300 billion barrels of proven reserves. Venezuela has the world's largest proven oil reserves, but production has been constrained for years by underinvestment, deteriorating infrastructure, sanctions and the nationalization of foreign-owned assets. The identity of the private operator involved in the joint venture has not yet been disclosed. Companies including Chevron, Repsol and Eni still have operations or interests in Venezuela, while other major oil companies remain wary after having assets nationalized under Hugo Chávez. The deal is part of a broader U.S. effort to reopen Venezuela's oil industry to foreign investment following the January U.S. military operation that removed Nicolás Maduro and installed Delcy Rodríguez as interim president. Source: https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-venezuela-oil-u-s-majority-control-65-billion-barrels/

headline: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth is considering bringing hundreds of senior military leaders back to Marine Corps Base Quantico for another address later this year, according to U.S. officials. Hegseth held a similar meeting there last September, when he summoned generals and admirals on short notice to outline his priorities for the force. The event focused heavily on warfighting, physical and grooming standards, and reversing diversity and inclusion policies from the previous administration. Officials say a second Quantico meeting would likely be used to outline additional priorities and issue new directives, although the date and exact attendance have not been determined. The Pentagon says it has nothing to announce at this time. It also remains unclear whether President Trump would attend, as he did last year. The potential meeting comes as Hegseth continues efforts to reshape military policies around physical standards, appearance and what he describes as a renewed focus on warfighting. Critics have argued that the administration's emphasis on these issues risks diverting attention from broader readiness and modernization challenges. Source: https://www.wsj.com/politics/policy/pete-hegseth-general-meeting-quantico-560cc230?mod=hp_lead_pos4

headline: Federal authorities are preparing potential charges against a U.S. servicemember accused of making more than $1 million in profits from Polymarket bets tied to military operations, according to people familiar with the investigation. The servicemember, who has been under scrutiny since the spring, allegedly made successful bets involving the timing or outcomes of U.S. military strikes in Iran and Venezuela. The case is part of a broader federal investigation into whether military personnel used confidential information to trade prediction-market contracts. A separate investigation involves a KPMG employee accused of betting on whether a public company would beat quarterly earnings expectations, potentially using nonpublic information obtained through their employment. Charges in both cases could come this fall, although prosecutors have not made final decisions. The investigations involve the Justice Department, federal prosecutors in Manhattan and Washington, and the CFTC. The cases are part of a broader effort to determine how existing insider-trading and financial-fraud laws apply to prediction markets such as Polymarket. Previous prosecutions involving alleged insider trading on the platform are already facing challenges over whether those laws apply to prediction-market contracts. Notably, the servicemember has not been charged at this point. The allegations remain under investigation. Source: https://www.wsj.com/finance/regulation/u-s-servicemember-kpmg-employee-are-targets-of-prediction-markets-crackdown-ec7fdd04?mod=e2tw
